official.deadline_note: First-ever AFdoc call, launched mid-September 2026. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, the second launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET.
official.status_note: The FNR instrument page lists the deadline as 25-11-2026 14:00 CET with a further deadline of 28-04-2027 14:00 CET for the 2027 cycle, and states that the very first call will be launched mid-September 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition fees and related research costs are not eligible.
benefits: Maximum annual salary contribution of EUR 54,574 per funded doctoral candidate, including employer charges, social security and pension contributions, based on the salary index applicable on 1 June 2026.
Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training.
Funding is granted to eligible Host Institutions, which employ the selected doctoral candidates as beneficiaries through an employment contract.
Eligible Host Institutions are public PhD-awarding institutions abroad, or Luxembourg-based private companies active in R&D and accredited by the Minister responsible for the Economy.
eligibility: Applicants must demonstrate a link to Luxembourg, be enrolled in a PhD programme by the project start date, not already hold a PhD, and not benefit from an old-age pension.
Each applicant may submit one proposal per call.
Bottom-up approach: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible.
In company-based projects, the doctoral research must involve collaboration with a public-sector PhD awarding institution such as the University of Luxembourg or a university abroad.
requirements: Applications must be submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System.

Eligible proposals are assessed on the scientific quality and potential of the project, the applicant's profile and potential, the quality of the Host Institution, supervision and training environment, and the expected impact of the project.

Projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities, provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner.
Submit no more than one proposal per call.
documents: Application guidelines AFdoc, published in the AFdoc call documents folder on the FNR SharePoint.

AFdoc PhD Project Description Template (Word and PDF versions), published in the AFdoc call documents folder.
COMMITMENT LETTER template, published in the AFdoc call documents folder.
selection_criteria: Scientific quality and potential of the project.
Quality of the Host Institution, supervision and training environment.
coverage: Maximum annual salary contribution of EUR 54,574 per funded doctoral candidate, including employer charges, social security and pension contributions.
Up to four years of doctoral training.
Tuition fees and related research costs are not eligible.
application_method: Prepare the proposal using the AFdoc call documents (application guidelines, selection guidelines, project description template and commitment letter).
Submit the proposal in English through the FNR Grant Management System at https://grants.fnr.lu/login.
Submit no more than one proposal per call.
Wait for the funding decision: March of the following year for the September call, July for the February call.
official.application_route: Submit in English through the FNR Grant Management System (https://grants.fnr.lu/login) using the AFdoc templates before the published 14:00 CET deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must demonstrate a link to Luxembourg; the full definition of that link is set out in the AFdoc guidelines. No nationality requirement is published.
official.international_eligibility: Eligible Host Institutions include public PhD-awarding institutions abroad, so a PhD hosted outside Luxembourg is eligible provided the applicant demonstrates a link to Luxembourg and, for company-based projects, collaborates with a public PhD-awarding institution.
official.research_requirement: A doctoral research project falling within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner; no thematic restriction is published.
official.duration: Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training.
official.description: Following the entry into force of the new FNR law on 1 August 2026, the Luxembourg National Research Fund is launching AFdoc - Aides a la formation doctorale, a PhD funding scheme supporting talented doctoral candidates with a clear link to Luxembourg who undertake PhD projects in established research environments abroad or through collaborations involving Luxembourg-based R&D companies.
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System.

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage and travel_coverage - the FNR publishes a maximum annual salary contribution but makes no explicit statement about living costs or travel, and individual award values below the ceiling are not published
study_mode - no full-time or part-time rule is published on the instrument page
the exact definition of 'link to Luxembourg' - the instrument page refers to the guidelines for the full definition and the call documents are hosted on an FNR SharePoint folder
verification.notes: The FNR AFdoc instrument page was read in full: the EUR 54,574 maximum annual salary contribution based on the 1 June 2026 salary index, the up-to-four-year duration, the 'tuition fees and related research costs are not eligible' rule, the 25 November 2026 14:00 CET deadline and the two-call-per-year pattern from 2027 were all confirmed on the FNR's own domain.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a salary, not a stipend: the FNR gives the money to your host institution, which then employs you, so you will be on an employment contract rather than receiving a bursary. The ceiling is EUR 54,574 a year including employer charges, but the actual figure is set per project, so the published maximum is not a promise. Tuition and research costs are explicitly excluded, so if your host charges doctoral fees you need a second source of money. The very first call closes on 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, and from 2027 the scheme moves to two calls a year with April and November deadlines.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Master's graduate with a demonstrated link to Luxembourg who wants a funded, employed PhD at a public university abroad or with a Luxembourg R&D company partnered to a PhD-awarding institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the AFdoc guidelines to check whether your personal link to Luxembourg meets the FNR's definition - the instrument page only summarises it.
Secure your host and supervisor early: the Host Institution must be a public PhD-awarding institution abroad or an accredited Luxembourg R&D company.
For company-based projects, confirm the collaboration with a public PhD-awarding institution is documented before you submit.
Make sure you will be enrolled in the PhD programme by the project start date, not just admitted.
Build the budget around the EUR 54,574 employer-inclusive ceiling and be explicit that tuition and research costs sit outside it.
Work on the AFdoc project description template and the COMMITMENT LETTER, then submit in English through grants.fnr.lu well before 14:00 CET on deadline day.
common_rejection_risks: Not being able to evidence a link to Luxembourg as the FNR defines it in the guidelines.
Not yet holding a PhD but already receiving an old-age pension, which is an explicit exclusion.
A host that is neither a public PhD-awarding institution abroad nor an accredited Luxembourg R&D company.
A company-based project without a documented collaboration with a public PhD-awarding institution.
Budgeting tuition or research costs into the award, which the FNR states are not eligible.
Submitting more than one proposal in the same call.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees and related research costs are not eligible and must be funded elsewhere. The salary contribution is also a ceiling: if the host institution's employment cost model exceeds EUR 54,574 a year, the difference between the indexed salary and the FNR contribution has to be met by the host.
document_audit: The call documents sit in an FNR SharePoint folder rather than on the instrument page, so download the application guidelines, selection guidelines, project description template and commitment letter from there before starting.
The COMMITMENT LETTER is a separate required piece from the host, not a line you write yourself.
The application must be in English; French or German drafts will not do for the submission system.
Only one proposal per applicant per call is allowed, so choose the host carefully.
alerts: The first-ever call closes on Wednesday 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET - this is a brand-new scheme, so there is no past-round precedent to calibrate against.

From 2027 the scheme runs two calls a year: decisions in July for the February call and in March for the September call, with funded projects starting no later than 1 February and 1 October respectively.
The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects, so expect that topic in the application.
A webinar hosted by ACEL and FNR took place on 10 September 2026; its materials are the quickest way to pick up the 'link to Luxembourg' definition.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You prepare the proposal on the AFdoc templates with your host's commitment letter, submit it in English through the FNR Grant Management System by the 14:00 CET deadline, and the FNR assesses project quality, applicant potential, host quality and impact before communicating its funding decision - March for the September call, July for the February call.
